A. CMESC's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for the Proposed Rule Change
(a) Purpose
The purpose of the proposed rule change is to (i) clarify the treatment of Haircut Collateral in Clear to Hold Transactions, (ii) modify the Rules regarding accounts and banks that Participants may use to settle deliverable obligations in Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions, (iii) modify the description of CMESC's daily settlement reports, including the content of such reports, to reflect CMESC's netting practice with respect to settlement obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions, (iv) clarify and update the descriptions of the settlement obligations and processing in existing Rules to more align with CMESC's settlement practices with respect to Eligible Securities Transactions, (v) update the descriptions of Outstanding Exposure Settlement calculations and processes for Eligible Securities Transactions, (vi) update settlement fails provisions, and (vii) make certain other technical, administrative, clarifying and conforming changes to ensure consistency and improve clarity and readability of the Rules.
Specifically, CMESC proposes to:
1. Amend Rules 503(b) and 101 to better describe certain features of Haircut Collateral in Clear to Hold Transactions;
2. Amend Rules 601, 604, 1504(c) and 101 to provide Participants with a wider range of options for banks used to settle securities delivery obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions;
3. Amend Rules 1504(e) and 101 regarding CMESC's daily settlement reports, including updated descriptions to reflect CMESC's practice with respect to netting settlement obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions;
4. Amend Rules 1504(d), (f) and (g) to consolidate duplicative text and revise the descriptions of settlement and netting procedures for Clear to Deliver Transactions, Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Hold Transactions for greater consistency, while also amending Rule 1504(f) to permit CMESC to settle obligations resulting from a same-day settling Cash Treasury Transaction or Clear to Deliver Transaction directly with the Participant counterparties to a riskless principal, without delivering securities or making payment to the riskless principal, where the riskless principal and its Participant counterparties have identical and offsetting settlement obligations, and amending Rule 1504(f)(v) to clarify certain operational timelines;
5. Amend Rule 1505 to update the description of CMESC's calculation and processing of Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Eligible Securities Transactions, including:
a. Amending Rules 1505(a) and 1505(d) to update the description of Outstanding Exposure Settlement calculation and process for Clear to Hold Transactions;
b. Amending Rules 1505(b), 1505(c) and 1505(f) to update the description of Outstanding Exposure Settlement calculation and processing for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions; and
c. Amending Rule 1505(b)(ii) to address processing for atypical trades such as transfers and related cash adjustments;
6. Amend Rule 1506 to update partial settlement fails provisions for both Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions and for Clear to Hold Transactions, including amending Rule 1506(h) to restrict CMESC's buy-in rights only to Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions; and
7. Make certain other technical, administrative, clarifying and conforming changes to ensure consistency and improve clarity and readability of the Rules.
The proposed rule change does not impact CMESC's risk management practices or related policies. Rather, it serves to clarify and update operational processes to provide certain details that were not previously provided. Each of the proposed changes is described in more detail below.
Description of the Proposed Rule Change
1. Amendments to Rule 503(b) To Clarify Treatment of Haircut Collateral in Clear To Hold Transactions and Rule 101 To Clarify the Meaning of Haircut Collateral
CMESC proposes several non-substantive changes to Rule 503(b)(i) to clarify the treatment of Haircut Collateral for Clear to Hold Transactions. First, CMESC proposes to clarify the meaning of the first sentence in Rule 503(b)(i), which currently provides that if Participants who are parties to a Clear to Hold Transaction have calculated and posted Haircut Collateral with respect to such transaction to the Securities Settlement Bank, CMESC will deem such Haircut Collateral as pledged to CMESC. CMESC proposes to clarify this statement by further providing that that if a Participant who is a party to a Clear to Hold Transaction has posted Haircut Collateral to CMESC, CMESC will deem such Haircut Collateral as pledged to CMESC to secure obligations of the posting Participant to CMESC, by changing “If Participants who are parties to a Clear to Hold Transaction have posted Haircut Collateral . . .” to “If a Participant who is a party to a Clear to hold Transaction has posted Haircut Collateral . . .”, deleting “calculated and” and adding “to secure obligations of the posting Participant to the Corporation” to the first sentence of Rule 503(b)(i).
In addition, CMESC proposes to further clarify the meaning of the second sentence in Rule 503(b)(i) to provide that CMESC will collect initial margin for each Participant for Clear to Hold Transactions novated to CMESC on a portfolio basis, rather than calculating and collecting initial margin on each individual transaction submitted for clearance and settlement, in order to better reflect CMESC's batch processing and portfolio-based margining processes as described in its documentation. Rule 503(b)(i) is being amended to provide that CMESC will “then calculate and collect initial margin for each Clear to Hold Transaction submitted” to CMESC “for clearance and settlement”, by adding “For each Participant,” and “Transactions novated” to the second sentence of Rule 503(b)(i) and removing “then calculate and”, “each” and “for clearance and settlement” from the second sentence.
The above changes do not change CMESC's practices for calculating each Participant's initial margin requirement or its treatment of Haircut Collateral posted by a Participant to the Securities Settlement Bank to secure such Participant's obligation to CMESC with respect to a Clear to Hold Transaction. These changes are intended to update descriptions in the Rulebook to better align with CMESC's initial margin practices and provide greater certainty regarding its treatment of Haircut Collateral.
Separately, CMESC proposes to amend the definition of “Haircut Collateral” in Rule 101 to clarify that “Haircut Collateral” means the “market” value of the Eligible Securities that the securities buyer receives under a Repo Transaction in excess of the value of funds the securities buyer

2. Amendments to Rules 601, 604, 1504(c) and 101 With Respect to Securities Settlement Bank Arrangements and Accounts With Settlement Bank(s)
CMESC proposes to amend Rules 601, 604, 1504(c) and 101 with respect to settlement bank arrangements for settling Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions and with respect to Securities Settlement Bank arrangements for settling Clear to Hold Transactions. Under existing Rule 604, all Members and Users must utilize the Securities Settlement Bank(s) that CMESC has designated to settle Eligible Securities Transactions. Rule 604(a) provides that CMESC must disclose to Members and Users the Securities Settlement Bank(s) it has designated to deliver and receive cash and Eligible Securities for the purpose of settlement. Under Rule 604(b), Members and Users must notify CMESC of their accounts at the designated Securities Settlement Bank(s).
CMESC proposes to amend Rule 604 (revised as “Banks for Settling Transactions”) to provide Members and Users a greater choice of banks they may use to settle delivery obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions with CMESC's Securities Settlement Bank(s), while clarifying that for Clear to Hold Transactions, Members and User must use the CMESC-designated Securities Settlement Bank(s). Specifically, CMESC proposes to amend Rule 604(a) as follows:
Establish separate requirements for the Securities Settlement Bank(s) that CMESC will designate and disclose to its Participants for settlement of different types of Eligible Securities Transactions: “(i) where the Corporation will hold accounts for the purpose of delivering” cash and Eligible Securities to and “receiving” cash and Eligible Securities from “Participants to settle Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions” and “(ii) where the Corporation and Participants may hold accounts for the purpose of delivering cash and Eligible Securities to and receiving cash and Eligible Securities from one another to settle Clear to Hold Transactions and to hold Eligible Securities as collateral for such transactions.” These changes maintain distinct settlement processes for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions on the one hand and Clear to Hold Transactions on the other hand, while clarifying that for purposes of settling Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions, the Securities Settlement Bank designated by CMESC will hold CMESC's accounts and Participants are not required to maintain settlement accounts at the same designated Securities Settlement Bank, while for purposes of settling Clear to Hold Transactions, the Securities Settlement Bank designated by CMESC will hold both CMESC's and Participants' accounts; and
Add a new sentence to Rule 604(a), consistent with the revisions outlined above, to permit Members and Users in Clear to Deliver and Cash Treasury Transactions to choose their banks for settlement, subject to satisfaction of certain conditions and CMESC's discretion to reject the Member's or User's choice of bank(s) due to operational or risk management considerations: “Each Member and User that will clear Cash Treasury Transactions or Clear to Deliver Transactions may establish its accounts to facilitate settlement of such transactions at one or more banks or trust companies, provided that the bank or trust company is subject to supervision under Federal or State banking laws and has access to the Fedwire for securities and funds movements, provided further that the Corporation may, in its reasonable judgment, reject a bank or trust company as notified by a Participant to facilitate settlement of Cash Treasury Transactions or Clear to Deliver Transactions due to operational or risk management considerations and require the Participant to establish its account(s) at a different bank or trust company meeting the criteria set forth above.”
As a result of the proposed changes to Rule 604(a), CMESC also proposes to make conforming changes to Rule 604(b) as follows:
Amend the first sentence of Rule 604(b) to specify that each Member and User must notify CMESC of the Securities Settlement Bank(s) “(for Clear to Hold Transactions) or the banks or trust companies (for Cash Treasury Transactions and/or Clear to Deliver Transactions), as applicable” that will act on its behalf with respect to handling settlement of Eligible Securities Transactions;
Amend the second sentence of Rule 604(b) to clarify that each Member and User “that will clear Clear to Hold Transactions” is required to enter into an agreement with a Securities Settlement Bank from a list of institutions designated by CMESC for the settlement of “such transactions.”; and
Add a new sentence to the end of Rule 604(b) to expand the existing notification requirement in Rule 604(b) regarding any change in a Member's or User's Securities Settlement Bank: “Each Member and User must immediately notify the Corporation of any change, as applicable, in any of its Securities Settlement Banks for settling and holding collateral for Clear to Hold Transactions or in any of the banks or trust companies where it maintains accounts to facilitate settlement of its Cash Treasury Transactions or Clear to Deliver Transactions.”
CMESC proposes to update the definition of “Securities Settlement Bank” in Rule 101 to conform to the proposed Rule 604 changes. Specifically, CMESC proposes to delete the reference to “and designated by” from the general definition and add language to clarify that a Securities Settlement Bank is a bank or trust company at which CMESC “maintains one of more accounts” for the purposes of facilitating the settlement of Eligible Securities Transactions and/or for holding collateral for Clear to Hold Transactions, as applicable. In addition, CMESC proposes to add new language to the definition to account for the requirement that “a Member or User maintains one or more accounts at a Securities Settlement Bank pursuant to the Rules for the purposes of facilitating the settlement of and holding collateral for Clear to Hold Transactions.” These amendments ensure that the definition applies to institutions through which Participants settle (i) Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions; and (ii) Clear to Hold Transactions.
Further, CMESC also proposes to amend Rule 601 by adding new language to clarify that, in addition to the Accounts with CMESC, each Member and User also “must establish accounts with one or more Banks in accordance with Rule 507 and accounts with one or more Securities Settlement Banks or other banks or trust companies in accordance with Rule 604, as pre-conditions” to clearing Eligible Securities Transactions with CMESC, which replaces the existing language that provides “accounts for settlement of Eligible Securities Transactions as specified and approved by the Corporation as a pre-condition”. These proposed changes are designed to set out the requirements for establishing accounts at one or more Banks for each Participant to satisfy initial margin and Outstanding Exposure Settlement requirements and for establishing

accounts at Securities Settlement Bank(s) and/or other banks or trust companies for purposes of settling Eligible Securities Transactions, in accordance with the revisions to Rule 604 described above.
Finally, CMESC also proposes to make conforming changes to Rule 1504(c) regarding “Settlement Accounts” to reflect the expansion of the Member's or User's settlement bank choice as described above. Specifically, CMESC proposes to delete existing language in Rule 1504(a) that requires a Participant to establish “a settlement account at the Corporation's Securities Settlement Bank for the relevant transactions” and “[f]or Members and Users that are cash lenders, such Members and Users must establish a collateral account in its name and for its exclusive benefit at the Corporation's Securities Settlement Bank.” CMESC proposes to add new language to require a Member or User to establish “accounts in accordance with the requirements of Rule 604 for the purposes of delivering cash and Eligible Securities to and/or receiving cash and Eligible Securities from the Corporation.” In addition, CMESC proposes to amend the last sentence in Rule 1504(c) to clarify that each Member and User is required to make available to CMESC upon request copies of its “agreement with any Securities Settlement Bank” and remove the existing requirement imposed on a Member or User to provide, upon CMESC's request, copies of its settlement account and collateral account agreements, as applicable.
3. Amendments to Rules 1504(e) and 101 on the Description of Daily Settlement Reports
CMESC proposes to amend existing Rule 1504(e) regarding daily settlement reports to better reflect CMESC's settlement and netting practices, including its processes for calculating net settlement obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions. First, CMESC proposes to clarify that it will issue multiple daily settlement reports by adding new language to the first sentence to provide that CMESC will issue one or more settlement reports daily and define such settlement reports in the aggregate as “Daily Settlement Reports.” Further, CMESC proposes to revise the description of the content of the Daily Settlement Reports to clarify that the Daily Settlement Report will indicate whether the obligations and entitlements listed therein relate to Clear to Hold Transactions or “to the settlement of deliverable” Clear to Deliver Transactions and “Cash Treasury Transactions” to reflect the practice set forth in Rule 1504(g) with respect to determining net settlement obligations of Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions that are scheduled to settled on the Business Day referenced in the Daily Settlement Reports. In addition, CMESC proposes to remove “with respect to Clear to Deliver Transactions, whether settlement shall occur on a real-time gross basis or on a net basis” to align with the updated description of the Daily Settlement Reports' content. Finally, CMESC proposes to change “Daily Settlement Report” in the last sentence to “Daily Settlement Reports” to reflect that there will be multiple settlement reports issued on each Business Day.
As a result of the proposed changes to Rule 1504(e) described above, which includes defining the term “Daily Settlement Reports,” CMESC proposes to add “Daily Settlement Reports” to Rule 101, where the term is defined as having the meaning prescribed in Rule 1504(e).
4. Amendments to Rule 1504(d), (f) and (g) To Consolidate Duplicative Text and Update the Descriptions of Settlement and Netting Procedures for Clear To Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions and for Clear To Hold Transactions
A. Amendments to Rule 1504(d)
CMESC proposes to amend Rule 1504(d) to consolidate duplicative text. Currently, Rule 1504(d) provides that CMESC will settle same-day Repo Transactions in real time on a gross basis and will settle Cash Treasury Transactions and other Repo Transactions that settle other than same-day on a net basis, and with respect to Clear to Hold Transactions, CMESC will net settlement obligations only against additional Clear to Hold Transactions in the same General Collateral Bucket with the same scheduled settlement date. Because the procedures for settlement and netting of Eligible Securities Transactions are described in further detail in Rule 1504(f) and (g), CMESC proposes to simplify Rule 1504(d) and eliminate duplicative provisions by replacing the current rule text in its entirety with a new sentence stating that “The Corporation may settle Eligible Securities Transactions in real time or on a deferred basis and may net settlement obligations in accordance with the procedures for settlement and netting of Clear to Hold Transactions and for Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions in Rules 1504(f) and (g) below.”
B. Amendments to Rule 1504(f)
CMESC further proposes to amend its description of settlement procedures with respect to Eligible Securities Transactions in Rule 1504(f) as follows:
First, CMESC proposes to amend Rule 1504(f)(i) to clarify that, in addition to Clear to Deliver Transactions, Cash Treasury Transactions may also be submitted for same day (T+0) settlement. Both types of transactions will be processed and settled in real time on a gross basis. Further, CMESC proposes to provide a riskless principal transaction exception from the real-time gross settlement of same-day (T+0) Clear to Deliver Transactions and/or Cash Treasury Transactions in Rule 1504(f)(i), to allow CMESC to settle the obligations resulting from two offsetting Clear to Deliver Transactions or Cash Treasury Transactions for same-day (T+0) settlement having the same CUSIPs, same purchase price and same Participant acting as riskless principal in each offsetting transaction by settling directly with the other Participants that face the riskless principal in the offsetting transactions without delivering securities or making payment to the riskless principal. This approach eliminates unnecessary operational steps involving the riskless principal and CMESC by allowing for the settlements of cash and securities to occur between CMESC and the counterparties to the riskless principal. Finally, CMESC is proposing a conforming change to Rule 1504(f)(i) to clarify that it will instruct its Securities Settlement Bank to effect movement of collateral securities against cash upon receipt of securities from the Member's or User's settlement bank(s), as notified by the Member or User to CMESC pursuant to Rule 604(b), in accordance with the changes outlined above regarding Participants' greater choice of bank(s) for purposes of settling Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions.
Second, CMESC proposes to amend Rule 1504(f)(ii) to make several conforming and clarifying changes to the description of settlement of Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions on a deferred basis, for which settlement obligations will be determined on a net basis pursuant to Rule 1504(g). Specifically, CMESC proposes to clarify in two places in Rule 1504(f)(ii) that Rule 1504(f)(ii) applies to all Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions submitted for deferred settlement,
i.e.,
settlement other than on the same day, which is not limited to T+1 settlement as reflected in the current Rules. Further,

CMESC proposes to clarify throughout Rule 1504(f)(ii) that the settlement instructions CMESC will issue to its Securities Settlement Bank for settlement on the next eligible settlement date are for the net settlement obligation resulting from the aggregate of each Participant's Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions that are scheduled for delivery on the next eligible settlement date, rather than on the basis of “netted” transactions which is potentially ambiguous in meaning. CMESC is amending the final paragraph of (f)(ii) to require the Corporation's Securities Settlement Bank(s) to notify CMESC upon completion of the settlement of Clear to Deliver Transactions, Cash Treasury Transactions or the combination of both types of transaction, which is a more precise restatement of the legacy requirement to notify CMESC “upon the settlement of any netted Clear to Deliver Transaction”. Existing Rule 1504(f)(iii) provides that CMESC will instruct its Securities Settlement Bank(s) to move securities against cash once Members and Users have “funded their cash and security obligations in their settlement accounts at the Corporation's Securities Settlement Banks.” CMESC proposes to adjust the last sentence in Rule 1504(f)(iii) to state that CMESC will instruct its Securities Settlement Bank(s) to move securities against cash once Members and Users have satisfied their cash and securities obligations by transferring cash and securities to CMESC's settlement accounts at its Securities Settlement Bank(s), which better reflects the distinct operational steps and contingencies for settling Clear to Hold Transactions.
Fourth, CMESC proposes to make several changes to Rule 1504(f)(v) to update the descriptions regarding various deadlines for submissions, processing and settlement of Eligible Securities Transactions. Specifically, CMESC proposes to:
Modify Rule 1504(f)(v)(G) to clarify that the 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time settlement deadline on each Business Day applies to both Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions submitted for same day (T+0) settlement, rather than only Clear to Deliver Transactions, which supports CMESC's processes for netting settlement obligations resulting from both transaction types. The modifications will also clarify that the same 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time deadline applies to the net collateral settlement obligations for the aggregate of Members' and Users' other Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions scheduled to settle on that Business Day, rather than other Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions from the previous Business Day, which is consistent with CMESC's proposed change to Rule 1504(f)(ii) to clarify that transactions submitted for deferred settlement are not limited only to T+1 settlement;

Make clarifying changes to Rule 1504(f)(v)(K) regarding CMESC's calculation of net collateral settlement obligations for each Participant at approximately 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on each Business Day to better describe CMESC's settlement practice. CMESC proposes to clarify in Rule 1504(f)(v)(K) that it will calculate each Participant's net collateral settlement obligation resulting from the aggregate of such Participant's Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions that are scheduled to settle the next Business Day. These changes are consistent with proposed changes to Rules 1504(f)(ii) and 1504(f)(v)(G) described above. C. Amendments to Rule 1504(g)

First, with respect to netting of cash delivery and securities settlement obligations for Clear to Hold Transactions, CMESC does not propose to change any substantive aspect of its procedures but proposes to clarify that cash or securities delivery and receipt entitlements for a given Business Day will be netted only by General Collateral Bucket for those Clear to Hold Transactions in which the Member or User is acting in the same capacity (
e.g.,

add “for a given Business Day” to Rule 1504(g)(ii)(C) to clarify that for those Clear to Hold Transactions in which a Member or User is acting as a cash lender, CMESC will determine the Member's or User's cash delivery obligations and receipt entitlement for a given Business Day;
replace “which begin on a given Business Day” in Rule 1504(g)(ii)(C)a. and b. with “in the same General Collateral Bucket which are scheduled to settle on that Business Day” to make clear that, for a given Business Day, CMESC's will determine a Member's or User's cash delivery obligation as a cash lender based on the aggregate of all Clear to Hold Transactions in the same General Collateral Bucket which are scheduled to settle on that Business Day; and
add “for each General Collateral Bucket” to Rule 1504(g)(ii)(C)c. to make clear that CMESC will net the amounts in Rules 1504(g)(ii)(C)(a)-(b) to determine a net cash settlement delivery obligation or receipt entitlement for each General Collateral Bucket with respect to those Clear to Hold Transactions in which the Member or User is acting as a cash lender.
In terms of netting the securities delivery obligations and receipt entitlements for Clear to Hold Transactions, CMESC proposes implementing clarifying changes to Rules 1504(g)(iii)(A), (B) and (C) that mirror the proposed changes to Rules 1504(g)(ii)(A), (B) and (C) described above with respect to the netting of cash delivery obligations and receipt entitlements for Clear to Hold Transactions. As a result of implementing these changes to Rules 1504(g)(iii)(A), (B) and (C), for Clear to Hold Transactions, the Rules will clarify how a Member's or User's securities delivery obligations will be netted against its securities receipt entitlements within the same General Collateral Bucket that are scheduled to settle on the same Business Day. Accordingly, CMESC proposes to delete the last sentence of Rule 1504(g)(iii)(B)c. to eliminate redundancy.
Second, with respect to netting of settlement obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transaction, similar to the revised descriptions of netting procedures for Clear to Hold Transactions, CMESC does not propose to change any substantive aspect of the procedures for netting cash and securities settlement obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions, but proposes to make a number of similar clarification changes to Rule 1504(g)(iv). Specifically, CMESC proposes to:
Add to Rule 1504(g)(iv)(A) “and determine the corresponding net cash settlement obligation for the aggregate for the resulting net collateral settlement obligations” and “and the associated cash settlement obligation” and “for a given Business Day” to clarify that CMESC will net a Member's or User's cash and securities settlement obligations each Business Day for obligations to be settled on the next eligible Settlement Date by netting the Clear to Deliver Transaction Start Leg collateral settlement obligations, Clear to Deliver Transaction Off Leg collateral settlement obligations, and Cash Treasury Transaction collateral settlement obligations to determine the net collateral settlement obligations and the corresponding net cash settlement obligations, and then CMESC will determine a Member's or User's netted collateral delivery obligation and receipt entitlement (
i.e.,
the net collateral settlement obligation) per CUSIP, and the associated cash settlement obligation for each clearing account for a given Business Day by following the procedures described in Rule 1504(g)(iv)(A)a. to e. These revisions are intended to clarify the operational steps that apply where CMESC aggregates certain Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions of a given Participant to determine its net settlement obligation;
Replace “for settlement on a given” Business Day to “to settle on that” Business Day in Rule 1504(g)(iv)(A)a. and b. to comport with the phrase “for a given Business Day” in rule 1504(g)(iv)(A) and make clear that, with respect to a given Business Day, CMESC's determination of the amount of a Member or User's netted collateral delivery obligation and the amount of its netted collateral receipt entitlement is with respect to the deliverable transactions that are scheduled to settle on that Business Day;
Replace “transactions” with “Cash Treasury Transactions and/or Clear to Deliver Transactions” and replace “an obligation” to “a collateral settlement obligation” in Rule 1504(g)(iv)(A)c. to clarify that “transactions” refer to Cash Treasury Transactions and/or Clear to Deliver Transactions” and “an obligation” refers to “a collateral settlement obligation” resulting from such transactions on a standalone or combined basis, as applicable; and

5. Amendments to Rule 1505 To Update the Description of Outstanding Exposure Settlement Calculation and Processing for Eligible Securities Transactions
CMESC proposes to amend Rule 1505 to update the descriptions of Outstanding Exposure Settlement calculations and processes for Clear to Deliver Transactions, Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Hold Transactions, as well as the description of the form and components of Outstanding Exposure Settlement that is paid to or received from Members and Users during the intraday clearing cycle. Each of the proposed changes to Rule 1505 is described below.
First, CMESC proposes to amend Rule 1505(a) regarding Outstanding Exposure Settlement in general by adding a sentence with respect to the form(s) of Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Hold Transactions, to provide that Outstanding Exposures Settlement obligations will be met in the form(s) permitted by CMESC and the relevant Securities Settlement Bank(s). This amendment provides that acceptable forms for Outstanding Exposure Settlement must be permitted by CMESC and as well as the relevant Securities Settlement Bank(s) to ensure
(
printed page 75621)
that collateral acceptance operations remain aligned as between CMESC and its Securities Settlement Bank(s).
Second, with respect to Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Deliver Transactions, CMESC proposes to make the following amendments to Rule 1505(b):
With respect to the settlement variation component of the Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Deliver Transactions described in Rule 1505(b)(i), CMESC proposes to:
clarify in Rule 1505(b)(i) that the loss or profit that will be paid to or collected from CMESC as a settlement variation payment is represented by the difference between the settlement prices for the applicable clearing cycles, multiplied by the par amount of the securities, instead of the difference between the settlement prices for the current and preceding clearing cycles, to reflect the practice that, for the first clearing cycle after novation of a Clear to Deliver Transaction, the settlement variation payment amount is represented by the difference between the current settlement price versus the price at which the Start Leg was purchased or sold, multiplied by the par amount of the securities;
add a sentence to Rule 1505(b)(i) to explain that the settlement variation payment amount for settlement cycles subsequent to the first settlement cycles shall be represented by the difference between the settlement price determined during the current settlement cycle versus the settlement price determined during the previous settlement cycle, multiplied by the par amount of the securities;
clarify that the accrued coupon interest included in the settlement price for Clear to Deliver Transactions is for the Business Day on which the settlement variation is to be settled, rather than the Business Day on which the settlement variation is calculated, by changing the word “calculated” to “to be settled” in the fourth sentence of Rule 1505(b)(i);
change the phrase “Where a Cash Treasury Transaction is netted against another obligation” in the fifth sentence of Rule 1505(b)(i) to “Where the Corporation settles one or more Cash Treasury Transactions and/or Clear to Deliver Transactions on a net basis as provided in Rule 1504(g)” to further clarify CMESC's processes for settling Cash Treasury Transaction obligations and Clear to Deliver Transaction obligations on a net basis as provided in Rule 1504(g);
clarify in the same fifth sentence of Rule 1505(b)(i) that CMESC will calculate settlement variation based on the resulting net delivery settlement obligation and subsequent settlement variation calculations for subsequent settlement cycles will use the settlement price for the net delivery settlement obligation determined during the previous settlement cycle as the starting price, by adding “resulting net”, “for subsequent settlement cycle”, “net”, “determined during the previous settlement cycle” to the fifth sentence of Rule 1505(b)(i); and
clarify in the last sentence of Rule 1505(b)(i) that the Haircut Collateral amount will be subtracted from the par amount of the securities (instead of settlement value), when determining the settlement value,
i.e.,
settlement price multiplied by the par amount of the securities for each calculation of the settlement variation.
With respect to the Repo Rate accrual component of the Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Deliver Transactions described in Rule 1505(b)(ii), CMESC proposes to:
add “Except as otherwise provided in the Rules, the” to the third sentence of Rule 1505(b)(ii) to account for certain special situations with respect to the calculation of daily repo rate accrual, such as transfers of positions between Accounts as described below; and
add a new sentence to the end of Rule 1505(b)(ii) to account for transfers of positions between Accounts pursuant to the Rules, in which case the aggregate repo rate accrual from the start date to the transfer date may be processed alongside a contrary cash adjustment at the time of the transfer.
With respect to the Price Alignment Amount component of the Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Deliver Transactions described in Rule 1505(b)(iv), CMESC proposes to clarify the timing of resetting the calculation for the Price Alignment Amount in Rule 1505(b)(iv)(C). Currently, Rule 1505(b)(iv)(C) provides that the calculation of the Price Alignment Amount will be reset when a transaction is netted against another obligation for settlement. CMESC proposes to clarify that the Price Alignment Amount calculation will be reset when CMESC settles obligations resulting from Clear to Deliver Transactions and/or Cash Treasury Transactions on a net basis in accordance with Rule 1504(g) as described above so that the Price Alignment Amount calculation will be based on the resulting net settlement obligation. CMESC proposes to clarify its process by removing the phrase “when a transaction is netted against another obligation for” from Rule 1505(b)(iv)(C) and adding “Where the Corporation settles one or more Clear to Deliver Transactions and/or Cash Treasury Transactions on a net basis as provided in Rule 1504(g),” and “such that it is based on the resulting net settlement obligation” to Rule 1505(b)(iv)(C). In addition, CMESC also proposes to remove the word “only” and add the word “net” to the last part of Rule 1505(b)(iv)(C) so it is clear that any subsequent Price Alignment Amount calculations will include settlement variation received or paid related to the net delivery settlement obligation.
With respect to Haircut Collateral collected or returned as part of the Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Deliver Transactions described in Rule 1505(b)(vii), CMESC proposes to make two clarification changes in Rules 1505(b)(vii)(A) and (B). CMESC proposes to clarify that collection of Haircut Collateral will be reflected as a debit of the “current cash value” of Haircut Collateral submitted on the transaction for the funds borrower and a credit for the funds lender by adding the words “current cash value of” and removing the word “cash” from Rule 1505(b)(vii)(A). Conversely, return of Haircut Collateral will be reflected as a debit of the “current cash value of” Haircut Collateral submitted on the transaction for the funds lender and a credit for the funds borrower and CMESC proposes to add to Rule 1505(b)(vii)(B) the words “current cash value of” and removing from Rule 1505(b)(vii)(B) the word “cash” to make this clarification.
Third, with respect to Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Cash Treasury Transactions, CMESC proposes to make the following amendments to Rule 1505(c)(i):
Add a sentence to Rule 1505(c)(i), similar to the sentence added to Rule 1505(b)(i), that states: “For subsequent settlement cycles for open Cash Treasury Transaction positions, the settlement variation payment amount shall be represented by the difference between the settlement price determined during the current settlement cycle versus the settlement price determined during the previous settlement cycle, multiplied by the par amount of the securities.” This revision reflects CMESC's approach to processing and calculating settlement variation for Cash Treasury Transactions in the same manner as Clear to Deliver Transactions for each settlement cycle;
Change the phrase “Where a Cash Treasury Transaction is netted against another obligation” in Rule 1505(c)(i) to “Where the Corporation settles one or more Cash Treasury Transactions and/or Clear to Deliver Transactions on a net
(
printed page 75622)
basis as provided in Rule 1504(g)” to clarify that settlement obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions will be determined on a net basis as provided in Rule 1504(g); and
Clarify that in circumstances where settlement obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and/or Clear to Deliver Transactions are determined on a net basis as provided in Rule 1504(g), CMESC will calculate settlement variation based on the resulting net delivery settlement obligation and subsequent settlement variation calculations for subsequent settlement cycles will use the settlement price for the net delivery settlement obligation determined during the previous settlement cycle as the starting price. CMESC proposed to make this clarification by adding “resulting net”, “for subsequent settlement cycle”, “net”, “determined during the previous settlement cycle” to the last sentence of Rule 1505(c)(i).
Fourth, with respect to Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Hold Transactions, CMESC proposes to make the following amendments to Rule 1505(d):
Revise reference from “subparagraphs (i)-(iii)” to “subparagraphs (i)-(v)” to account for new paragraphs (iv) and (v) added to Rules 1504(d), as discussed below;
Add the phrase “subject to applicable procedures of the Corporation and the Corporation's Securities Settlement Bank(s).” to clarify that the permitted forms of Outstanding Exposure Settlement will be subject to the applicable procedures of CMESC and the Securities Settlement Bank(s), in order to maintain consistency with the revised text of Rule 1505(a); and
Address two additional components of the Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Hold Transactions by adding two new subparagraphs (iv) and (v) to Rule 1505(d) regarding the exchanges of Outstanding Exposure Settlement and a transfer cash component or cash adjustment amount that may be included in Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Hold Transactions:
Proposed new Rule 1505(d)(iv) will provide that the Settlement Variation component of Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Hold Transactions will be exchanged at least twice daily in the form of Eligible Securities collateral and at times that coincide with the processing of Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions set forth in Rule 508(c)(i) and (ii), except as otherwise permitted by CMESC and applicable procedures of the relevant Securities Settlement Bank; and
Proposed new Rule 1505(d)(v) will provide that Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Hold Transactions that are subject to a delivery failure, default management or transfers may include a transfer cash component or other miscellaneous cash adjustment amount to be paid or collected, at the CMESC's instruction and on the timelines consistent with the Clear to Deliver timeline for settling Outstanding Exposure Settlement, through a Bank or a Securities Settlement Bank designated by CMESC.
Fifth, with respect to intraday clearing cycle on each Business Day, CMESC proposes to amend Rule 1505(f)(i) to provide more detail with respect to the form(s) and components of Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions. Currently, Rule 1505(f)(i) provides that Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions will be exchanged and will only be inclusive of the settlement variation calculation as detailed in Rule 1505. CMESC proposes to clarify that Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions will be exchanged “in cash unless otherwise determined or permitted by the Corporation, will include the settlement variation calculation as detailed in this Rule 1505, and may include other cash adjustments as determined by the Corporation, including repo rate accrual adjustments in special cases involving the transfer or close out of relevant transactions.”
Finally, CMESC also proposes certain technical, administrative, clarifying and conforming changes to Rule 1505(f) that are not described above. Please see the descriptions in the table under “7.

6. Amendments to Rules 1506 To Update Settlement Fails Provisions for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear To Deliver Transactions and for Clear To Hold Transactions
CMESC further proposes to amend Rule 1506 to update and clarify settlement fail provisions for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions and for Clear to Hold Transactions as follows:
First, with respect to Repo Transaction fails, CMESC proposes to add “for Clear to Deliver Transactions” to Rule 1506(b)(iii) and Rule 1506(c)(ii) to clarify that the fail charge assessed against a Member or User that failed to deliver Eligible Securities in satisfaction of the settlement obligations with respect to the Start Leg or Off Leg a Repo Transaction would not apply to Clear to Hold Transactions.
Second, CMESC proposes to delete clause (ii) from Rule 1506(d) regarding Cash Treasury Transaction Fails, because repo rate assessment would not apply to Cash Treasury Transactions, and to renumber existing clause (iii) as clause (ii) due to that deletion.
Third, CMESC proposes to amend existing Rule 1506(f) to clarify that fail charges are assessed against a failing Member or User only with respect to Clear to Deliver Transactions or Cash Treasury Transactions. CMESC proposes to make this clarification by replacing the reference to “Repo” Transactions with “Clear to Deliver” Transactions in the first sentence of Rule 1506(f) and adding “for Clear to Deliver Transactions or Cash Treasury Transactions” to the second sentence of Rule 1506(f) to clarify that CMESC will pay collected fail charges “for Clear to Deliver Transactions or Cash Treasury Transactions” pro rata to the Members or Users to which CMESC allocates the fail.
Fourth, CMESC also proposes to amend Rule 1506(g) for partial deliveries of settlement obligations. Existing Rule 1506(g) outlines the procedural requirements in the event that a Member or User fails in part to satisfy its obligation to deliver Eligible Securities to settle a Repo Transaction or Cash Treasury Transaction. CMESC proposes to amend Rule 1506(g) to include two subparts: (1) proposed Rule 1506(g)(i) would apply to Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions, and (2) proposed Rule 1506(g)(ii) would apply to Clear to Hold Transactions. Specifically:
Existing Rule 1506(g) would become new Rule 1506(g)(i), applicable to Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions, with the following modifications:
Because the first sentence of existing Rule 1506(g) describes the same requirements that are now provided in Rule 1504(f)(viii)(B), to eliminate redundancy, CMESC proposes to remove the first sentence of existing Rule 1506(g) and add to the second sentence of existing Rule 1506(g) (which now becomes Rule 1506(g)(i)) a cross reference to “in accordance with the provisions of Rule 1504(f)(viii)(B)”;
Replace “Repo” Transaction with “Clear to Deliver” Transaction in the second sentence of exhibit Rule 1506(g) (now the first sentence of new Rule
(
printed page 75623)
1506(g)(i)) to clarify that the applicable Repo Transaction being referred to is Clear to Deliver Transaction, not a Clear to Hold Transaction; and
Replace “Repo” Transaction with “Clear to Deliver” Transaction “or a Cash Treasury Transaction” in the third sentence of existing Rule 1506(g) (now the second sentence of new Rule 1506(g)(i)) to clarify that, if a Member or User partially fails to satisfy its obligation to deliver Eligible Securities to settle the Start Leg or Off Leg of a Clear to Deliver Transaction or a Cash Treasury Transaction, CMESC's obligation to deliver Eligible Securities to the Member or User allocated the fail shall be reduced.
New Rule 1506(g)(ii) for Clear to Hold Transaction will provide the following:
First, with respect to a Member or User's failure to settle the Start Leg of a Clear to Hold Transaction, new Rule 1506(g)(ii) will allow for partial delivery subject to certain conditions, as follows: “In the event that a Member or User fails in part to satisfy its obligation to deliver Eligible Securities to settle the Start Leg of a Clear to Hold Transaction, the Corporation will allow for partial delivery of an obligation; provided that such partial deliveries comply with the rules, policies, procedures and practices of the Corporation and the relevant Securities Settlement Bank(s) and Bank(s) used to settle such obligations.”; and
The procedures for partial delivery for Clear to Hold Transactions in new Rule 1506(g)(ii) will be added, as follows: “If a Member or User delivers Eligible Securities in an amount that partially satisfies its obligation to deliver Eligible Securities to settle the Start Leg of a Clear to Hold Transaction, (x) the Corporation shall deliver such Eligible Securities to the Member or User allocated the fail, and (y) the failing Member or failing User will receive cash equal to the value of Eligible Securities delivered. If a Member or User partially fails to satisfy its obligation to deliver Eligible Securities to settle the Start Leg of a Clear to Hold Transaction, the Corporation's obligation to deliver Eligible Securities to the Member or User allocated the fail shall be reduced by the amount of the failing Member's or failing User's unsatisfied delivery obligation, until the Business Day on which the Corporation has received such Eligible Securities from the failing Member or User. If the Corporation delivers Eligible Securities to the Member or User allocated the fail to settle the Start Leg of a Clear to Hold Transaction in an amount that partially satisfies the Member's or User's securities receipt entitlement with respect to such Repo Transaction, the Member's or User's obligation to deliver Eligible Securities to the Corporation on the Off Leg of such Repo Transaction shall be reduced by the amount of the Member's or User's unsatisfied securities receipt entitlement.”
Fifth, CMESC proposes to amend Rule 1506(h) (revised to refer to “Corporation Buy-in; Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions”) to limit CMESC's buy-in rights to Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions by adding a new lead-in phrase “With respect to Cash Treasury Transactions and/or Clear to Deliver Transactions:” to clarify that Rule 1506(h) applies to only to Clear to Deliver Transactions and Cash Treasury Transactions and does not apply to Clear to Hold Transactions. In addition, CMESC proposes to make the following clarifying and clean-up changes to Rule 1506(h):
Replace “loaned to” with “owed by” in Rule 1506(h)(i) to improve clarity and readability;
Replace “borrowed from” with “owed by” in two places in Rule 1506(h)(iii) and changing “was the cash borrower” to “is the failing party” in the same paragraph to improve clarity and readability, as well as consistency across CMESC documentation; and
Amend the last sentence of Rule 1506(h)(iv) to provide more detail regarding the actions CMESC will take to effect a cash settlement on the first Business Day after CMESC receives a notice of the value of the securities from a Member or User that effects a cash settlement. CMESC proposes to replace “pay such” with “collect from the failing Member or failing User, and pay to the non-failing” and to add “, as determined by the Corporation,” and “non-failing” to the last sentence, which will provide: “On the first Business Day after the Corporation receives such notice, the Corporation shall collect from the failing Member or failing User, and pay to the non-failing Member or User, any reasonable loss or cost, as determined by the Corporation, incurred in connection with such cash settlement, and such non-failing Member or User shall pay the Corporation any profit or gain made in connection therewith.”

(b) Statutory Basis
CMESC believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act. Section 17A(b)(3)(F) requires, in part, that the rules of a clearing agency be designed to promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a national system for the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
[
5
]
The proposed changes to Rules 503(b), 1503, 1504, 1505 and 1506 are designed to better describe certain features of and clarify CMESC's treatment of Haircut Collateral in Clear to Hold Transactions, as well as to clarify and update descriptions of CMESC's settlement fails provisions, its processes for settling Eligible Securities Transactions and for calculating and processing Outstanding Exposure Settlement, to better align with CMESC's operational processes and the practices of the Securities Settlement Bank(s), as applicable, and to enhance consistency and transparency. In addition, the proposed changes to Rule 604 and the associated conforming changes to Rules 601 and 101 will expand Participants' choice of settlement bank(s), subject to CMESC's discretion with respect to operational and risk management considerations. As such, CMESC believes that the proposed rule change will facilitate the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions, which, in turn, promotes the protection of investors and the public interest, in furtherance of Section 17A(b)(3)(F).
[
6
]
In addition, CMESC also believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Rule 17ad-22(e)(9),
[
7
]
which requires each covered clearing agency to establish, implement, maintain, and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to conduct its money settlements in central bank money, where available and determined to be practical by the Board, and minimize and manage credit and liquidity risk arising from conducting its money settlements in commercial bank money if central bank money is not used. Under the proposed changes to Rule 604 and the associated conforming changes to Rules 601 and 101, CMESC will provide Participants with greater choice of banks used to settle securities delivery obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions, provided that such bank or trust company is subject to supervision under Federal or State banking laws and has access to the Fedwire for securities and funds movements. In addition, CMESC may, in its reasonable judgment, disallow a Participant from utilizing a bank or trust company for settling its Eligible Securities Transactions due to operational or risk management considerations. The conditions imposed on the settlement bank(s) chosen by Participants are designed to minimize and manage credit and liquidity risk arising from money settlements in commercial bank money. As such, CMESC believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of Rule 17Ad-22(e)(9).
[
8
]
Finally, CMESC believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Rule 17ad-22(e)(12), which requires a covered clearing agency, for transactions that involve the settlement of two linked obligations, to establish, implement, maintain and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to eliminate principal risk by conditioning the final settlement of one obligation upon the final settlement of the other, regardless of whether the covered clearing agency settles on a gross or net basis and when finality occurs. As stated above, the proposed rule change serves to clarify and update operational processes to provide certain details that were not previously provided and does not impact CMESC's risk management practices. In particular, the proposed rule change does not increase any principal risk for CMESC in the clearance and settlement process. CMESC's existing Rule 1504 already requires the settlement of Eligible Securities Transactions on a delivery versus payment basis, effectively conditioning the final settlement of the securities delivery obligation(s) upon the final settlement of cash payment, regardless of whether the Eligible Securities Transactions are settled on a gross or net basis. Proposed amendments to Rules 1504(d), (f) and (g) would consolidate duplicative text and revise the descriptions of settlement and netting procedures for Clear to Deliver Transactions, Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Hold Transactions for greater consistency in conditioning the final settlement of the securities delivery obligation upon the final settlement of the cash payment obligation, whether on gross or net basis. In addition, proposed amendments to Rule 1504(f) would permit CMESC to settle obligations resulting from a same-day settling Cash Treasury Transaction or Clear to Deliver Transaction directly with Participant counterparties to a riskless principal, without delivering securities or making payment to the riskless principal, where the riskless principal and its Participant counterparties have identical and offsetting settlement obligations, which
(
printed page 75626)
will promote settlement efficiency without increasing or changing CMESC's principal risk. Similarly, proposed amendments to Rule 1506 also do not change or increase CMESC's principal risk, which is eliminated under the existing Rules that already provide allocation of fails and partial delivery, but are designed to update and clarify settlement fail provisions for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions and for Clear to Hold Transactions. As such, CMESC believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of Rule 17ad-22(e)(12).
B. CMESC's Statement on Burden on Competition
CMESC does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change does not impact CMESC's risk management practices or related policies. Rather, it serves to clarify and update operational processes to provide certain details that were not previously provided. As such, the proposed rule change does not change Participants' access to CMESC's Clearing Services or Participants' delivery or payment obligations for purposes of settlement or create additional rights and obligations of Members and Users that do not already exist under the existing Rules and other existing risk management policies. As such, CMESC does not believe the proposed rule change would have impact on burden on competition that does not already exist under the existing Rules or other existing risk management policies or is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
C. CMESC's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
CMESC currently does not have any Members or Users and has not received nor solicited any written comments from others related to this proposal. CMESC has not received any unsolicited written comments from any interested parties. If any written comments are received, they will be publicly filed as Exhibit 2 to this filing, as required by Form 19b-4 and the General Instructions thereto.
Persons submitting comments are cautioned that, according to Section IV (Solicitation of Comments) of the Exhibit 1A in the General Instructions to Form 19b-4, the Commission does not edit personal identifying information from comment submissions. Commenters should submit only information that they wish to make available publicly, including their name, email address, and any other identifying information.
All prospective commenters should follow the Commission's instructions on how to submit comments, available at
https://www.sec.gov/​regulatory-actions/​how-to-submit-comments
.
General questions regarding the rule filing process or logistical questions regarding this filing should be directed to the Main Office of the Commission's Division of Trading and Markets at
tradingandmarkets@sec.gov
or 202-551-5777. CMESC reserves the right to not respond to any comments received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not:
(i) Significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest;
(ii) Impose any significant burden on competition; and
(iii) Become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
9
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
10
]
thereunder.
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views, and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules-regulations/​self-regulatory-organization-rulemaking
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include File Number SR-CMESC-2026-009 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, Station Place, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549.
All submissions should refer to File Number SR-CMESC-2026-009. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules-regulations/​self-regulatory-organization-rulemaking
). Copies of the filing also will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of CMESC and on CMESC's website (
https://www.cmegroup.com/​market-regulation/​rule-filings.html
). Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to File Number SR-CMESC-2026-009 and should be submitted on or before December 14, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.

Office of the Secretary
AGENCY:
Office of the Secretary, HHS.
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
The Federal Medical Assistance Percentages (FMAP) and Enhanced Federal Medical Assistance Percentages (eFMAP) for fiscal year 2028 have been calculated pursuant to the Social Security Act (the Act). These percentages will be effective from October 1, 2027, through September 30, 2028. This notice announces the calculated FMAP rates, in accordance with the Act, that the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will use in determining the amount of Federal matching for State medical assistance (Medicaid), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) Contingency Funds, Child Support collections, Child Care Mandatory and Matching Funds of the Child Care and Development Fund, Title IV-E Foster Care Maintenance payments, Adoption Assistance payments and Kinship Guardianship Assistance payments, and the eFMAP rates for the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) expenditures. Table 1 gives figures for each of the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. This notice reminds states of adjustments available for states meeting requirements for disproportionate employer pension or insurance fund contributions and adjustments for disaster recovery. At this time, no state qualifies for such adjustments, and territories are not eligible.
DATES:
The percentages listed in Table 1 will be effective for each of the four quarter-year periods beginning October 1, 2027, and ending September 30, 2028.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Amelia Whitman, Office of Health Policy, Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation, Room 447D—Hubert H. Humphrey Building, 200 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20201, (202) 578-1478.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The Secretary of HHS manages programs under titles IV, XIX and XXI of the Act in each jurisdiction of the United States. Programs under titles I, X, and XIV of the Act operate only in Guam and the Virgin Islands, and a program under title XVI of the Act (Aid to the Aged, Blind, or Disabled) operates only in Puerto Rico. The percentages in this notice apply to State expenditures for most medical assistance and child health assistance, and assistance payments for certain social services provided under these titles. The Act provides separate terms for Federal matching of administrative costs.
Sections 1905(b) and 1101(a)(8)(B) of the Act require the Secretary of HHS to publish the FMAP rates each year. The Secretary calculates the percentages, using formulas set out in sections 1905(b) and 1101(a)(8), and calculations from the Department of Commerce of average income per person in each State and for the United States (meaning, for this purpose, the fifty states). The final percentages are subject to upper and lower limits specified in section 1905(b) of the Act. The percentages for the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands are specified in statute, and thus are not based on the statutory formula that determines the percentages for the 50 states.
Federal Medical Assistance Percentage
Section 1905(b) of the Act, subject to statutory qualifications, specifies the formula for calculating FMAPs as follows:
(
printed page 75518)
“[T]he term `Federal medical assistance percentage' for any State shall be 100 per centum less the State percentage; and the State percentage shall be that percentage which bears the same ratio to 45 per centum as the square of the per capita income of such State bears to the square of the per capita income of the continental United States (including Alaska) and Hawaii; except that (1) the Federal medical assistance percentage shall in no case be less than 50 per centum or more than 83 per centum[.]”
Section 1905(b) further specifies that the FMAP for Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, and American Samoa shall be 55 percent. However, section 5101(b) of Division FF of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 (
Pub. L. 117-328
) amended section 1905(ff) of the Act to provide that the FMAP for the Virgin Islands, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, and American Samoa shall be 83 percent permanently. We note that the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 also amended section 1905(ff) of the Act to provide that the FMAP for Puerto Rico shall be 76 percent through September 30, 2027. Beginning October 1, 2027, the FMAP for Puerto Rico will be 55 percent under section 1905(b)(2) of the Act. In addition, we note that the rate that applies for Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, and Guam in certain other programs pursuant to section 1118 of the Act is 75 percent. Section 4725(b) of the Balanced Budget Act of 1997 (
Pub. L. 105-33
) amended section 1905(b) to provide that the FMAP for the District of Columbia, for purposes of titles XIX and XXI, shall be 70 percent. For the District of Columbia, we note under Table 1 that other rates may apply in certain other programs. The rates for the states, the District of Columbia, and the territories are set out in Table 1, Column 1.
Section 1905(y) of the Act, as added by section 2001(a)(3) of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (“Affordable Care Act”) (
Pub. L. 111-148
), provides for an increase in the FMAP for medical assistance expenditures for newly eligible individuals described in section 1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(VIII) of the Act, as added by the Affordable Care Act (the adult group); “newly eligible” is defined in section 1905(y)(2)(A) of the Act. The FMAP for the adult group is 100 percent for Calendar Years 2014, 2015, and 2016, gradually declining to 90 percent for calendar quarters in 2020 and each year thereafter.
[
1
]
In addition, section 1905(z) of the Act, as added by section 10201 of the Affordable Care Act, provides that states that offered substantial health coverage to certain low-income parents and nonpregnant, childless adults on the date of enactment of the Affordable Care Act, referred to as “expansion states,” shall receive an enhanced FMAP beginning in 2014 for medical assistance expenditures for nonpregnant childless adults who may be required to enroll in benchmark coverage under section 1937 of the Act. Some of these provisions are discussed in more detail in the proposed rule, “Medicaid Program; Eligibility Changes Under the Affordable Care Act of 2010,” published on August 17, 2011 (
76 FR 51148
,
51172
) and the final rule and interim final rule published on March 23, 2012 (
77 FR 17144
,
17194
). This notice does not set forth the matching rates for the adult group as specified in section 1905(y) of the Act or the matching rates for nonpregnant, childless adults in expansion states as specified in section 1905(z) of the Act.
Other Adjustments to the FMAP
For purposes of title XIX (Medicaid) of the Act, the FMAP, defined in section 1905(b) of the Act, for each State beginning with fiscal year 2006, may be subject to an adjustment pursuant to section 614 of the Children's Health Insurance Program Reauthorization Act of 2009 (CHIPRA),
Public Law 111-3
.
First, the FMAP is adjusted if a State experiences no growth or positive growth in total personal income and an employer in that State has made a significantly disproportionate contribution to an employer pension or insurance fund. The adjustment involves disregarding the significantly disproportionate employer pension or insurance fund contribution in computing the per capita income for the State (but not in computing the per capita income for the United States). Employer pension and insurance fund contributions are significantly disproportionate if the increase in contributions exceeds 25 percent of the total increase in personal income in that State. A
Federal Register
Notice with comment period was published on June 7, 2010 (
75 FR 32182
) announcing the methodology for calculating this adjustment; a final notice was published on October 15, 2010 (
75 FR 63480
).
The second situation arises if a State experiences negative growth in total personal income. Beginning with fiscal year 2006, section 614(b)(3) of CHIPRA specifies that, for the purposes of calculating the FMAP for a calendar year in which a State's total personal income has declined, the portion of an employer pension or insurance fund contribution that exceeds 125 percent of the amount of such contribution in the previous calendar year shall be disregarded in computing the per capita income for the State (but not in computing the per capita income for the United States).
No Federal source of reliable and timely data on pension and insurance contributions by individual employers and states is currently available. We request that states report employer pension or insurance fund contributions to help determine potential FMAP adjustments for states experiencing significantly disproportionate pension or insurance contributions and states experiencing a negative growth in total personal income. See also the information described in the January 21, 2014
Federal Register
notice (
79 FR 3385
).
Section 1905(aa) of the Act, as amended by section 2006 of the Affordable Care Act, specifies that notwithstanding section 1905(b) of the Act, the FMAP for a “disaster-recovery FMAP adjustment State” is adjusted as described in section 1905(aa)(1) of the Act. The statute defines a “disaster-recovery FMAP adjustment State” as one of the 50 states or District of Columbia for which, at any time during the preceding 7 fiscal years, the President has declared a major disaster under section 401 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act, under which every county or parish in the State warrant individual and public assistance or public assistance from the Federal Government, and for which the regular FMAP
[
2
]
as determined for succeeding fiscal years is less than the FMAP for the preceding fiscal year by an amount outlined under sections 1905(aa)(2)(A) and (aa)(2)(B) of the Act. This notice does not contain disaster recovery adjustments since no state qualifies as a “disaster-recovery FMAP adjustment State.” See more information described in the December 22, 2010
Federal Register
notice (
75 FR 80501
).
(
printed page 75519)
Enhanced Federal Medical Assistance Percentage (eFMAP) for CHIP
Section 2105(b) of the Act specifies the formula for calculating the eFMAP rates as follows:
[T]he “enhanced FMAP”, for a State for a fiscal year, is equal to the Federal medical assistance percentage (as defined in the first sentence of section 1905(b)) for the State increased by a number of percentage points equal to 30 percent of the number of percentage points by which (1) such Federal medical assistance percentage for the State, is less than (2) 100 percent; but in no case shall the enhanced FMAP for a State exceed 85 percent.
The eFMAP rates are used in the Children's Health Insurance Program under title XXI and in the Medicaid program for expenditures for medical assistance provided to certain children as described in sections 1905(u)(2) and 1905(u)(3) of the Act. There is no specific requirement to publish the eFMAP rates. We include them in this notice for the convenience of the states (Table 1, Column 2).

. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties (CRCL) reviews and investigates civil rights and civil liberties complaints filed by the public regarding U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) policies and activities. Under
6 U.S.C. 345
and
42 U.S.C. 2000ee-1
, CRCL reviews and assesses allegations involving a range of alleged civil rights and civil liberties abuses.
The information collected on this form will allow CRCL to review and investigate civil rights and civil liberties complaints filed by the public regarding DHS programs and activities.
CRCL submits copies of all external allegations of civil rights and civil liberties violations within its jurisdiction that it receives to the DHS Office of Inspector General (OIG) for review because OIG has the right of first refusal to investigate any allegations. If the OIG declines to investigate the allegations, CRCL may investigate. CRCL coordinates with DHS Components and the OIG regarding matters that CRCL opens as complaint investigations as well as some it decides not to investigate. In general, CRCL shares the incoming information with the Components involved and coordinates with the Components throughout a CRCL investigation. CRCL typically has a designated liaison office or person for each component and directs requests to them, which they route or share according to their internal procedures and obligations to obtain and share information with CRCL pursuant to statute, delegation, and other Department policies and directives. CRCL staff receive privacy training and adhere to DHS required policies and procedures regarding the protection of PII. At the conclusion of its complaint investigations, CRCL may issue recommendations to DHS Components to address issues of concern and to enhance the agency's civil rights and civil liberties protections. CRCL also engages with Components on the implementation of such recommendations.
In addition, the information provided is entered into a CRCL complaint management system (CMS) and may be used by CRCL to track allegations and identify trends and systemic issues that are within CRCL's jurisdiction regardless of whether CRCL investigates an individual allegation. CRCL has used information from these database records to notify DHS Components of issue areas and locations that may warrant closer attention.
Information must be submitted to CRCL via the web form
https://www.dhs.gov/​make-civil-rights-complaint
and may be initiated by members of the public. The use of the complaint form is mandatory, but all fields do not have to be completed to submit a complaint.
The form in an electronic form and it is available online for submission at
https://www.dhs.gov/​make-civil-rights-complaint
.
This information collection does not have an impact on small businesses or other small entities.
If the information collection is not conducted or is conducted less frequently, CRCL may not be able to effectively fulfill its statutory obligation to the public to review and investigate allegations involving alleged civil rights and civil liberties concerns regarding DHS polices and activities.
The assurance of confidentiality provided to the respondents for this information collection will be provided by: CRCL's statute under
6 U.S.C. 345
,
42 U.S.C. 2000ee-1
; the Privacy Impact Assessment for the CRCL Complaint Form and Privacy Waiver; and the Systems of Record Notice: Department of Homeland Security/ALL-029 Civil Rights and Civil Liberties Records System of Records.
This submission is a reinstatement of a previously approved collection. Any changes reflected are updates made to incorporate 2026 data and information. No other program changes or adjustments have been made beyond these updates. This notice replaces the published notice, on July 22, 2026. The public will have 60 days from the publication date of this notice to submit comments on the collection.
The Office of Management and Budget is particularly interested in comments which:
1. Evaluate whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information will have practical utility;
2. Evaluate the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used;
3. Enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and
4. Minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology,
e.g.,
permitting electronic submissions of responses.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Introduction
The RFA
[
1
]
requires agencies to consider the effects of their regulatory actions on small entities. Section 610 of the RFA requires each agency to review all final rules that the agency has determined have, or will have, a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities, within 10 years of the publication of such final rules.
[
2
]
The purpose of the review is “to determine whether such rules should be continued without change, or should be amended or rescinded . . . to minimize any significant economic impact of the rules upon a substantial number of such small entities.”
[
3
]
The RFA further requires each agency to publish in the
Federal Register
a list of rules that are to be reviewed in accordance with Section 610 during the succeeding 12 months.
[
4
]
II. Results of the Review
The Commission includes in its rule review any rule that may have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities but excludes rules that previously have been reviewed, rules that have been substantially changed since adoption, rules that are minor amendments to previously adopted rules, and rules that are ministerial, procedural, or technical in nature.
Based upon an analysis of the rules adopted by the Commission in 2017, the Commission has determined that no rules are required to be reviewed pursuant to the RFA during the succeeding 12 months. Accordingly, the Commission is not publishing a list of rules to be reviewed pursuant to the RFA during the succeeding 12 months.
Issued in Washington, DC, on November 18, 2026, by the Commission.
Christopher Kirkpatrick,
Secretary of the Commission.
